Landing.tagline: Build your profile once, generate a tailored resume for every job posting.
Landing.intro: Your professional history is structured data, not a document. AtomCV keeps it that way, then produces a resume for each posting from that data — inside a page limit that is calculated rather than hoped for.

pageLimit.title: A page limit that holds
pageLimit.body: Every item's height is measured in the real template. Selection is solved as an optimization problem, so the limit is a constraint rather than a request.

deterministic.title: Same input, same output
deterministic.body: Scoring and selection run in code, not in a language model. Two runs of the same posting produce the same resume.

noInvention.title: Nothing invented
noInvention.body: The model never writes free content. It chooses from what you wrote and rewrites narrowly, and every rewrite is checked for lost numbers, changed names and added technologies.

formats.title: Content independent of format
formats.body: The same profile renders to PDF, DOCX or source. No formatting is baked into your data.

transparency.title: Reasons you can inspect
transparency.body: Every item shows its score and the keywords it matched. Content left out is listed and can be added back in one click.

Landing.openSourceNote: Free and open source under the MIT licence. Run by one person, with no service guarantee — if it is ever shut down, notice comes at least 30 days in advance.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.collectBody: Profile content taken from your CV, your email address, and usage metrics.
privacy.whyBody: To generate resumes, manage your account, and improve the service.
privacy.shareBody:
AI providers receive the content needed to analyse a posting and rewrite your own wording: the text of your CV, the postings you paste, the text of individual items, and the inputs to summaries and covering letters. That is personal data.

Requests go to OpenRouter, which brokers them to whichever provider is serving the model we use. For the model currently in use those are OpenAI, Microsoft Azure (its global, US and EU endpoints), Amazon Bedrock (us-east-1) and Google. A request names the model rather than a provider, and the answer does not say which one served it, so all of them are listed. They may also keep short-lived logs of those requests on their own side.

Every request is sent with data collection denied, which means it is not routed to a provider that may train on it. OpenRouter's own logging policy is separate from that and is set on our account. The model currently in use is openai/gpt-5.6-sol; this list follows the model, and is reviewed whenever the model changes.

The other processors we use: email delivery — Resend, which sends through AWS SES in the ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) region, so your address and the delivery metadata around it are processed outside the EU; file storage — Cloudflare R2; and sign-in with Google or GitHub, when you choose it. Analytics are anonymous and cookie-free.
privacy.retentionBody: Account data for as long as the account exists. Anonymous sessions expire two hours after your last activity (what you made in one is deleted from the database within five minutes of that, and can remain in encrypted backups for up to six months). Generated PDFs are kept 14 days, or indefinitely if you archive them. Logs are kept 30 days.
privacy.rightsBody: Access, correction, deletion, and export of your data in JSON and Markdown.
privacy.deletionBody:
Deleting your account removes your profile, every resume you generated and the documents they made, anything still queued, your usage counters, your email preferences, your sessions and your connected accounts. It is permanent and cannot be undone.

Two things are kept on purpose. What your generations cost us stays, with the link to you cut, so it no longer identifies anyone. And if your address ever hard-bounced or reported us as spam, that record stays — it belongs to the address rather than to the account, and deleting it would let us write to an address that told us not to.
privacy.contactBody: Contact details to be added before publication.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.noGuaranteeBody: AtomCV helps you present the experience you already have. It does not promise interviews or offers.
terms.estimate: The fit report is an estimate
terms.estimateBody: It shows how well your resume reflects the terms used in a posting. It does not reproduce the behaviour of any particular applicant tracking system, and real hiring decisions depend on far more than keyword coverage.
terms.accuracyBody: Review what you send. The generated document is built from content you provided, and you remain responsible for it.
terms.abuseBody: Accounts used to attack the service, to extract model output for unrelated purposes, or to generate content about people other than yourself may be suspended.
terms.noSlaBody: The service is free and offered as a personal project. There is no uptime guarantee and no support commitment. If it is discontinued, notice will be given at least 30 days in advance, and your data will remain exportable during that period.

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.anonymous: You are working without an account, so the settings above are the narrower set. <link>Sign in</link> for the rest of them.
Settings.emailsLabel: Send me the occasional email about my account
Settings.emailsNote: Two, and no more: a welcome note the first time you sign in, and a confirmation when an account is deleted. The confirmation is sent either way — being told your data has gone is not something we let you switch off. Sign-in links are not on this list; they answer something you just did.
Settings.deleteIntro: This removes everything you have here. It cannot be undone.
Settings.deleteConfirmBody:
This deletes your profile — {sections, plural, =1 {one section} other {# sections}} and {atoms, plural, =1 {one item} other {# items}} — along with {generations, plural, =0 {every resume you generate} =1 {the one resume you have generated} other {all # resumes you have generated}} and the documents they made, anything still queued, your usage counters and your email preferences. It cannot be undone.

Two things stay. Our record of what your generations cost is kept with the link to you cut, so it no longer shows anyone. And if your address ever bounced or reported us, that record stays with the address rather than with the account — deleting it would let us write to you again after being told not to.

The AI providers may hold their own short-lived logs on their side. The privacy policy says which.

Appearance.intro: This applies to every resume you generate from now on. It is not asked again per resume.

Unsubscribe.keeps: One email is not on this list and cannot be: if an account is ever deleted, the confirmation is still sent. Being told your data has gone is not something we let anyone switch off. Sign-in links are not optional either — they answer something you just did.
Unsubscribe.done: Done. The optional emails have been stopped.
